milestone: Resident GPU tensor results after reduction feedback
implementation: Bounded tensor-result graph proof accepts one or more contributing reductions, rank-one/rank-two float32 outputs, checked helpers and matrix products
Returned tensor is a graph result consumer; its immutable GPU buffer moves into a buffer-layout task after the final stage acknowledges
Reuses resident reduction buffers and direct/Tier 2 broadcast shaders; tensor results emit no final scalar join or scalar result readback
Host task metadata preserves tensor rank/shape for cached observations, explicit transfers and subsequent GPU tasks
Preflight validates roots, broadcast ordering, kernel signatures, complete shapes, residency, capture budgets and final tensor liveness
Strict reduction order and float32 arithmetic, acknowledged cancellation and allocation-failure cleanup remain unchanged

qualification.reference: Independent LLVM APFloat division and balanced-adjacent sums; tensor bits compared exactly except NaNs compared by classification
cases: Vector lengths 0,1,2,3,7,64,65,257; finite encodings, subnormals, signed zeros, infinities, quiet/signaling NaNs, cancellation-sensitive values and arbitrary float32 bits; ordinary/zero scale
Nonempty normalization submits exactly two GPU commands and empty normalization only the resident reduction command; result remains device-resident until explicit download
Cached result observations retain tensor ownership; allocation failure at each of 37 checkpoints; cancellation/deadline/device failure at both command stages publishes no result
Pending core destruction during either command waits for acknowledgement and releases owned buffers, captures and graph workspace
Malformed missing/forward/duplicate broadcasts fail before dispatch; unused source reductions retain transactional G001 rejection
Rank-two outputs, reversed scalar/tensor division, repeated normalization, tensor maps used only by a reduction, zero-scalar-parameter signatures and matrix products
A tensor map consuming 32 reduced scalars uses Tier 2; result can feed a separate GPU task with no intervening download
Ten CLI scenarios including relocated output, each executed with 1/2/4 workers in all four modes
Installed Release compiler builds tensor feedback; relocated programs continue working after compiler resources are removed

remaining: Wider GPU numeric types, broader tensor ranks and device control flow
Optimization: scalar last-use reclamation, scheduling, storage reuse and fusion
